what_happened: Two findings against the dispatch STATEMENT. (F1) ladderFrame's fwd hypothesis quantifies over the full carrier Q x N x N, but Rlad requires pend x.1 = false -> x.2.1 = 0, so an idle state with c = 1 has no successor, and if every state is pending (q,0,n) has none: fwd is unsatisfiable for every object, ladderFrame has never been instantiated (the ninth probe is generic over fwd/bwd), and ladderModel over ladderFrame cannot be built - Adm must be a carrier restriction. (F2) The stabilization statement over (c,n) >= |cl phi| is refuted on Q = Bool (pend = id, step total): the first idle after z carries n in [n-c-1, n+c+1], so n-c is observable via untl p (r and X(p and X r)), X := untl bot; cellAt (a,B,B+1) != cellAt (a,B,B+2); the past direction gives a second refutation (n < c-1 forces a pending-forever past, snce top r separates). Both the exhibited-B and exists-B forms fail. T1's positive verdict is one-region and never exercises n.

Both findings were machine-checked inside the research dispatch: prototype/ladder-cell-refutation-proto.lean (no_fwd, no_bwd_of_idle, cell_ne, exhibited_form_refuted, exists_form_refuted) compiles with 0 errors / 0 warnings in three guard-routed lake env lean rounds (~25 min), every headline theorem at [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] or less, no sorryAx. The only tactic friction worth remembering: omega cannot see < on F.Duration (ascribe the untl witness as (s : Z), per the fixture's truth_Xp idiom), and full simp [Count] rewrites Nat casts inside hypotheses (use rw with Count-on-concrete-Bool lemmas instead).

lean-challenge-snapshot.sh forces each theorem's chunk to ':= sorry' up to the NEXT matched declaration (theorem|lemma|def|instance), so any abbrev or anonymous instance that sits between two theorems is silently swallowed into the preceding sorry; its identifier regex is also ASCII-only, so Unicode-named declarations (phi, w1, w2 in the prototype) either escape the Goals cross-check or truncate. Worked around in the plan: all supporting definitions precede the first theorem as abbrevs, the four supporting facts the probe proves (RladAdm_fwd, RladAdm_bwd, fwdB, bwdB) are sorry-bodied abbrevs rather than Goals, and the probe renames φ/w₁/w₂ to phi/w1/w2. The assembled module was compiled through the build guard at plan time (0 errors, 9 expected sorry warnings). A --dry-run that also compiles the assembled module, and a Unicode-aware identifier regex, would remove both hazards.

lake-build-guard.sh build -- env lean FILE REPLAYED the previous invocation's stale result (errors citing line numbers of the OLD file contents) after FILE had been rewritten at the same path: the staleness fingerprint (stat mode) evidently does not cover an arbitrary file argument to 'env lean'. Worked around with --no-share (and, first, a renamed copy). A guard caller compiling a single file it has just edited must pass --no-share or the result is not evidence.

plan-format.md's final-phase rule (the final phase must depend transitively on EVERY other phase) has no provision for a pre-decided [BLOCKED] decision-gate phase: making the executable phases depend on a phase that is blocked at plan time would deadlock the implementer, while not depending on it violates the rule's letter. Resolved by placing the blocked gate in wave 1 beside the first executable phase with 'Depends on: none', stating in the wave-table note that the final phase re-observes the gate's measurement through the wired probe, and recording the lemma's blocked state at both the phase heading and (at return) the plan-level Status. Precedent plans (archive/006 plan 05, archive/008 plan 03) carry a Phase 1 [BLOCKED] the same way. A one-paragraph provision in plan-format.md's Decision gates subsection would settle this.

Both carried figures were re-derived at plan time rather than trusted: the research prototype re-compiled through the build guard (exit 0, zero warnings, the five #print axioms lines exactly as reported), and the plan's Lean Challenge Statements block was assembled by lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --dry-run and compiled fresh (--no-share) with 0 errors — so the statement pin the implementer will be held to is known to typecheck before implementation starts. validate-artifact.sh --strict passes with 0 warnings.

Phase 2 port of the research prototype into the wired probe compiled first time through lake-build-guard (exit 0, zero errors, zero warnings, five #print axioms lines exactly as the plan records); the three ASCII renames (phi/w1/w2) were applied by sed and left no residue. No plan-revision sentinel was present for Phase 2.

Phase 4 gate 'check-task-references.sh --quiet exits 0' fails with 198 pre-existing unexempted task-number citations, all under Boneyard/ (archived READMEs) and Tests/BimodalTest (109), none in any file this dispatch touched; the lint scoped to RaySummary/README.md, docs/theorem-index.md and scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh exits 0 for each. Recorded as a pre-existing repo-wide debt the plan's gate line did not anticipate, not as a regression.

Plan Phase 4's last task instructs the implementer to set the plan-level '- **Status**:' field to [BLOCKED]; the lean-implementation-agent contract (MUST NOT 15, plan-status-ownership) reserves that field for update-plan-status.sh via update-task-status.sh postflight. The agent followed the contract: the field was left untouched and the checklist item annotated as a deviation (skipped), with the blocked outcome carried through .return-meta.json (status partial, blocked_phase 1, requires_user_review) instead.

Phase 5: RunLayer's import closure does not reach TaskModel/Atom (unknown namespace FormalSystem.Syntax at first build); added import FormalSystem.Semantics.TaskModel (narrowest defining module) rather than AnchorLayer, which the plan excludes. Annotated on the Phase 5 checklist.

A plan-revision sentinel (revised_at 1791715037 > dispatch_start_ts 1791714772, dispatch_seq 5) landed in place while Phase 5 was [IN PROGRESS]: citations re-anchored to .dispatch/4-aux and 5-aux files and the out-of-scope section now names task 765; no phase added, removed, or re-marked. Phase 5's and Phase 6's steps re-read from the revised text and found unchanged; the revision's hunks were carried into the phase 5 commit together with the phase-5 marker edits.

Phase 6: check-module-invariants.sh --no-build exit 1 on two findings the plan did not anticipate: INV (three generated inventory blocks stale by the new module's file count) and C23 (RladAdm_fwd/RladAdm_bwd Uppercase_x). Fixed by --emit-inventory and by extending the script's class (c) leave-alone set; neither is a rename, the Challenge names stand.
